title: Peri-urethral calcifications as a potential biomarker for acute genitourinary toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Peri-urethral calcifications as a potential biomarker for acute genitourinary toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background and objectives · abstract-1-1】Peri-urethral calcifications (PUCs) are readily identifiable on planning computed tomography (CT) and may reflect chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and reduced peri-urethral tissue compliance. We evaluated whether baseline PUCs are associated with acute genitourinary (GU) toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Peri-urethral calcifications as a potential biomarker for acute genitourinary toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We retrospectively analyzed 60 consecutive patients with localized prostate adenocarcinoma treated with definitive SBRT between June 2023 and February 2026. PUCs were assessed on non-contrast planning CT using predefined criteria by blinded observers. The primary endpoint was acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity occurring during treatment or within 90 days, graded according to CTCAE v5. Associations with toxicity were evaluated using logistic regression, with Firth penalized regression used for multivariable analysis.

【Results · abstract-3-1】PUCs were identified in 17 patients (28.3%). Interobserver agreement was high (93.3%; Cohen's κ = 0.84). Overall, 21 patients (35%) developed acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity, including three (5%) with grade ≥ 3 toxicity. Acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity occurred significantly more frequently in patients with PUCs than in those without PUCs (64.7% vs 23.3%; OR 6.05, 95% CI 1.78-20.51; P = 0.006). After adjustment for baseline International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), PUCs remained independently associated with toxicity (adjusted OR 6.90, 95% CI 1.97-27.96; P = 0.002). Baseline IPSS was also independently associated with toxicity (adjusted OR 1.13 per point; P = 0.008).
